prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values and priorities
- Freedom, justice, honesty; green principles across all policies.
- Invest in schools and the NHS; more police; higher basic state pension; free personal care for the elderly.

Health
- Cut waiting times via 27,500 more nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, 10,000 extra beds, and pay boosts for low-paid staff.
- Prevention focus: more scanners; restore free dental/eye checks; NHS dentistry access.
- End charges for long-term personal care; create a Pharmaceutical Agency; move to scrap prescription charges; no-fault compensation; end mixed wards; ban age discrimination in care.
- De-bureaucratise the NHS; locally accountable governance.

Education, skills and work
- Primary classes averaged at 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants; paid prep time; ICT and books funding.
- Scrap SATs at 7; replace National Curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; reduce targets and Ofsted burdens.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorer students; fairer loan repayment threshold.
- Adult learning entitlements to Level 2 (to Level 3 for 16–24s); training incentives for SMEs; paid study leave for 16–24s; reform New Deal into a universal job-help guarantee.

Law and order
- 6,000 extra police; 2,000 part-time community officers; a Community Safety Force; independent police complaints system.
- Shift from prison expansion to rehabilitation, skills and work; more community sentences.
- Protect jury trial; end most mandatory sentences; stronger victims’ rights; tackle hate crime; youth justice reform; Royal Commission on drugs.

Transport
- Free off-peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim half-fares for under-19s in education.
- Abolish VED for the greenest cars; no real-terms fuel duty rise next Parliament.
- Stronger public control: create a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure Railtrack to a not‑for‑profit model; bonds and congestion charging powers for local investment; rural transport fund.

Pensions, benefits and low pay
- Raise basic state pension (more for over‑75s/80s); Independent Pensions Authority; long-term move to citizen entitlement; 50% income tax over £100k to fund pensions/NHS.
- Annual minimum wage review; single full rate from 16+; extra support for disabled people and children in long-term poverty; fairer utilities tariffs; restore benefits to 16–17s; tackle fuel poverty via home insulation.

Business, consumers and environment
- Cut red tape; small business rates allowance; stronger competition law; tighter bank regulation; consumer protections.
- Replace the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; 10% renewables by 2010 (rising annually); phase out nuclear over time; expand energy efficiency; stricter chemical and water standards.

Constitution and civil liberties
- Electoral reform: AV+ referendum for Westminster; STV for local/European elections; votes at 16.
- Replace Lords with an elected Senate; stronger Commons scrutiny; Civil Service Act; local income tax; more devolution and elected regional assemblies.
- Stronger Freedom of Information; Equality Act covering all discrimination grounds; repeal Section 28; humane, faster asylum system; judicial oversight of surveillance; no ID cards.

Communities, rural and housing
- One‑stop regeneration grants; national recycling (60% in 10 years) and doorstep collections; protect green spaces; brownfield-first development; fair planning of masts.
- Reform CAP/CFP for sustainability; support small/tenant farms and organics; Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, foreign policy and defence
- Pro‑EU reform: constitution clarifying powers; transparency; subsidiarity; enlargement; euro entry via referendum at a competitive rate.
- Human-rights‑led foreign policy; end arms export subsidies; back ICC and stronger UN; oppose US NMD; maintain defence spending; retain minimum nuclear deterrent; improve forces’ welfare.
